Zero-Cost PATI Infrastructure Build
START PATI — COMPLETE MASTER PROMPT You are responsible for researching, architecting, building, testing, securing, and continuously improving a system called PATI — Personal AI Tool Infrastructure. READ THIS ENTIRE PROMPT BEFORE TAKING ACTION. ================================================== ABSOLUTE REQUIREMENT #1 — EVERYTHING MUST BE FREE THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT RULE IN THIS ENTIRE PROJECT. I DO NOT WANT TO PAY FOR ANYTHING. I mean EVERYTHING. I do not want to pay for: AI APIs AI models GPU compute CPU compute cloud compute hosting databases storage inference image generation video generation voice generation speech recognition coding agents research APIs automation services API gateways plugins subscriptions credits deployment testing services monitoring background jobs queues or any other infrastructure required for PATI. COST = $0. This is NOT a preference. This is NOT “$0-first.” This is NOT “use free services where possible.” THIS IS A HARD ARCHITECTURAL REQUIREMENT. PATI MUST BE A ZERO-COST SYSTEM. MANDATORY POLICY: FREE_ONLY = TRUE PAID_SERVICES = FALSE PAID_APIS = FALSE PAID_MODELS = FALSE PAID_COMPUTE = FALSE PAID_HOSTING = FALSE PAID_STORAGE = FALSE PAID_DATABASES = FALSE PAID_FALLBACKS = FALSE AUTO_BILLING = FALSE CREDIT_CARD_REQUIRED = FALSE MAX_SPEND = 0 MAX_AUTOMATIC_SPEND = 0 Never silently introduce a paid dependency. Never activate billing. Never consume paid credits. Never tell me to subscribe just to make something work. Never recommend a paid solution simply because it is easier or faster. If something requires payment, it is NOT an acceptable core solution. If something only gives: free trials temporary credits introductory credits limited promotional access free credits that eventually expire free access requiring billing free access requiring a credit card pay-as-you-go pricing DO NOT classify it as genuinely free. Classify it appropriately and reject it as a core dependency. If no legitimate free resource can perform a task, return: RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE Do not spend money to hide the limitation. A slower free solution is preferable to a faster paid solution. A limited free solution is preferable to a paid solution. RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE is preferable to spending money. ================================================== WHY I AM BUILDING PATI I am not trying to build another simple AI wrapper. I am trying to build MY OWN AI INFRASTRUCTURE AND API. The purpose of PATI is to become the infrastructure layer that my Personal AI can use. Eventually I want to be able to expose my own PATI API to other users. The goal is to OWN THE INFRASTRUCTURE ABSTRACTION rather than continuously depending on somebody else’s paid AI API. My Personal AI should be able to say: “I need text generation.” PATI should determine: Which free model can do it? Where can it run? Is the worker available? Is quota available? Is the model legally usable? Is it installed? Is it healthy? Which option is best? Can multiple workers run the task? What happens if the first worker fails? Then PATI executes the task and returns the result. The architecture should therefore be: PERSONAL AI ↓ PATI API ↓ AUTHENTICATION ↓ AUTHORIZATION + POLICY ENGINE ↓ TASK ORCHESTRATOR ↓ PLANNER ↓ CAPABILITY ROUTER ↓ MODEL / TOOL / WORKER REGISTRIES ↓ RESOURCE SELECTOR ↓ FREE WORKER ↓ MODEL / TOOL / AGENT ↓ VALIDATION + QA ↓ ARTIFACT STORE ↓ RESULT ================================================== CORE DESIGN PRINCIPLES PATI must be: capability-first vendor-neutral provider-independent modular replaceable portable secure autonomous testable benchmarkable observable multi-tenant capable commercialization-ready Do not make one provider the permanent foundation. Do not make one model the permanent “brain.” Do not make one cloud provider the permanent compute layer. Do not make one database impossible to replace. Do not hard-code external providers into the core orchestration engine. Everything external must sit behind adapters. ================================================== RESEARCH BEFORE BUILDING DO NOT immediately start writing a huge amount of code. First perform deep, current research. Do not rely on memory when current information can be verified. For every important tool, model, framework, service, worker, protocol, platform, or infrastructure option, investigate: current availability actual free status free limits whether payment is required whether billing is required API availability automation capabilities self-hosting open-source status license commercial-use rights hardware requirements RAM requirements VRAM requirements GPU requirements Kaggle compatibility installation method operating-system compatibility authentication requirements rate limits storage limits session limits concurrency Terms of Service security implications maintenance status vendor lock-in last verified date Classify every resource as: FREE_FOREVER FREE_WITH_LIMITS FREE_TRIAL PAID OPEN_SOURCE_SELF_HOSTED UNKNOWN UNAVAILABLE Do not call something “free” simply because it offers free credits. ================================================== SOURCE QUALITY Prefer: 1. Official documentation 2. Official GitHub repositories 3. Official model cards 4. Official license pages 5. Official Terms of Service 6. Primary research papers 7. Reputable technical sources 8. Community discussions when necessary If sources disagree, investigate the disagreement. Do not guess. Do not invent APIs. Do not invent quotas. Do not invent pricing. Do not invent capabilities. ================================================== RESEARCH REPORT Create: RESEARCH_REPORT.md For every important candidate include: Technology Purpose Free status Open source Self-hostable API GPU requirement RAM requirement VRAM requirement Kaggle compatibility Commercial use License Limits Security Automation PATI role Recommendation Confidence Last verified For every major component choose: USE OPTIONAL DEFER REJECT Explain why. ================================================== CAPABILITY-FIRST ARCHITECTURE PATI must be built around capabilities instead of providers. Initial capabilities should include: TEXT: text_generation reasoning summarization translation structured_output classification extraction rewriting question_answering CODING: coding code_generation code_review debugging refactoring repository_analysis coding_agent test_generation documentation_generation architecture_generation RESEARCH: web_research document_research source_comparison fact_checking literature_research market_research technical_research research_synthesis VISION: vision image_understanding OCR document_vision image_captioning visual_question_answering IMAGE: image_generation image_editing image_to_image image_upscaling background_removal character_generation character_consistency VIDEO: text_to_video image_to_video video_to_video video_upscaling frame_interpolation video_editing storyboard_generation scene_generation character_consistency_video AUDIO: text_to_speech speech_to_text voice_conversion voice_generation lip_sync music_generation audio_processing AUTOMATION: browser_automation web_scraping filesystem_operations git_operations github_operations API_operations scheduled_tasks APP BUILDING: app_generation frontend_generation backend_generation database_generation testing browser_testing deployment CI_CD security_scanning INFRASTRUCTURE: container_execution GPU_execution batch_execution remote_execution artifact_storage benchmarking model_evaluation tool_evaluation ================================================== TARGET ARCHITECTURE Personal AI | v PATI API | v Authentication | v Authorization + Policy Engine | v Task Orchestrator | v Planner | v Capability Router | +–> Model Registry +–> Tool Registry +–> Worker Registry +–> Capability Registry +–> Quota Manager | v Resource Selector | +–> Local Worker +–> Kaggle Worker +–> Container Worker +–> Browser Worker +–> CPU Worker +–> GPU Worker +–> Image Worker +–> Video Worker +–> Audio Worker +–> Coding Worker +–> Research Worker +–> Deployment Worker | v Model / Tool / Agent | v Validation + QA | v Artifact Store | v Result + Logs + Provenance ================================================== LOCAL HARDWARE My local computer has limited hardware. Do not solve this by telling me to purchase hardware. The local machine should primarily handle: orchestration API routing registries database caching lightweight inference development Git configuration UI security metadata task management Heavy workloads should be delegated to legitimate free remote compute when available. ================================================== KAGGLE WORKER Investigate Kaggle deeply as a potential legitimate free GPU worker. Verify CURRENT official information. Research: GPU types GPU quotas session limits RAM storage internet access persistence notebook execution API CLI automation concurrency queue behavior Terms of Service legitimate orchestration methods Do not assume any quota. Kaggle must be treated as: EPHEMERAL BATCH COMPUTE NOT: PERMANENT VPS PERMANENT SERVER UNLIMITED GPU PATI’s Kaggle worker should: receive job prepare inputs select compatible runtime execute workload save artifacts report logs report resource usage return results clean up Quota management must be built into PATI. If Kaggle cannot legally or technically support a proposed workflow, do not build PATI around that workflow. ================================================== WORKER ARCHITECTURE Worker types: LOCAL_WORKER KAGGLE_WORKER CONTAINER_WORKER BATCH_WORKER REMOTE_FREE_WORKER OPTIONAL_CLOUD_WORKER BROWSER_WORKER CPU_WORKER GPU_WORKER VIDEO_WORKER AUDIO_WORKER IMAGE_WORKER CODING_WORKER RESEARCH_WORKER DEPLOYMENT_WORKER Every worker must expose: register health capabilities resources submit status cancel logs artifacts heartbeat shutdown ================================================== MODEL REGISTRY Every model should contain: model_id name organization provider version modality capabilities license license_url source_url repository_url model_url hardware_requirements RAM_requirement VRAM_requirement quantization_options context_length languages input_types output_types latency_estimate quality_score speed_score cost free_status availability worker_requirements startup_time cold_start_time max_context tool_calling_support structured_output_support vision_support reasoning_support commercial_use license_restrictions known_limitations benchmark_results last_verified status ================================================== TOOL REGISTRY Every tool should contain: tool_id name description category capabilities version source repository documentation license install_method runtime dependencies hardware_requirements network_requirements input_schema output_schema health_check benchmark_command security_profile sandbox_required worker_type startup_command shutdown_command status last_verified commercial_use free_status fallback_tools adapter ================================================== TASK SYSTEM Task fields: task_id tenant_id user_id parent_task_id capability priority input input_schema constraints policy selected_worker selected_model selected_tool execution_plan status progress created_at started_at completed_at error artifacts logs cost resource_usage retry_count trace_id metadata Statuses: QUEUED PLANNING ROUTING WAITING_FOR_RESOURCE RUNNING PAUSED VALIDATING COMPLETED FAILED CANCELLED QUARANTINED ================================================== INTELLIGENT ROUTER Score resources based on: capability_match quality reliability latency hardware_availability free_status quota_remaining license_compatibility commercial_compatibility privacy failure_rate startup_time resource_usage task_priority worker_health model_health historical_benchmark FREE resources receive priority. PAID resources are blocked. If no free resource exists: RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE ================================================== QUOTA MANAGER Track: GPU hours API requests worker availability storage bandwidth rate limits concurrency daily usage weekly usage monthly usage model quotas service quotas cooldowns queue depth ================================================== AUTONOMOUS TOOL DISCOVERY When PATI needs a capability that does not exist: DISCOVER ↓ RESEARCH ↓ VERIFY ↓ LICENSE CHECK ↓ SECURITY CHECK ↓ INSTALL ↓ SANDBOX ↓ HEALTH CHECK ↓ BENCHMARK ↓ COMPARE ↓ REGISTER ↓ ACTIVATE ↓ MONITOR ↓ REPLACE ↓ QUARANTINE Never blindly install or execute downloaded code. The system must be capable of discovering better free alternatives. ================================================== TOOL LIFECYCLE DISCOVERED RESEARCHING CANDIDATE APPROVED INSTALLING INSTALLED TESTING BENCHMARKING ACTIVE DEGRADED STALE QUARANTINED DEPRECATED REMOVED FAILED ================================================== ADAPTER SYSTEM Every external provider, model, service, or tool must be isolated behind an adapter. Adapter responsibilities: metadata capability declaration configuration installation health check execution result normalization error normalization cleanup license information security profile resource requirements Directories: adapters/README.md adapters/template/ adapters/llm/ adapters/coding/ adapters/image/ adapters/video/ adapters/audio/ adapters/research/ adapters/browser/ adapters/deployment/ adapters/database/ adapters/testing/ ================================================== MCP PATI should expose a secure MCP server and support MCP clients/adapters. Potential tools: pati_generate_text pati_generate_image pati_generate_video pati_research pati_run_code pati_build_app pati_deploy pati_search_tools pati_install_tool pati_run_worker pati_get_job pati_get_artifact pati_get_system_status Administrative tools require authorization. Never expose unrestricted shell or credential access. ================================================== VLLM Investigate vLLM as an optional model-serving adapter. Use compatible APIs where useful. Do not make vLLM a hard dependency. PATI remains the abstraction layer. ================================================== CODING AGENTS Agent roles: PRODUCT_AGENT SPEC_AGENT ARCHITECT_AGENT CODER_AGENT REVIEWER_AGENT TEST_AGENT DEBUGGER_AGENT SECURITY_AGENT DOCUMENTATION_AGENT DEPLOYMENT_AGENT Workflow: UNDERSTAND PLAN IMPLEMENT TEST REVIEW FIX RETEST DOCUMENT COMMIT Canonical: AGENTS.md Vendor-specific: CLAUDE.md GEMINI.md CODEX.md CURSOR.md COPILOT.md These must contain meaningful instructions and reference the canonical PATI architecture. ================================================== SECURITY Required: authentication authorization RBAC API keys service tokens scoped credentials tenant isolation secret isolation sandboxing SSRF protection command injection protection path traversal protection prompt injection defense tool poisoning defense supply-chain security dependency scanning license scanning malware scanning network restrictions filesystem restrictions CPU limits memory limits timeouts audit logs rate limits credential isolation production protection Never give external tools unrestricted access to: SSH keys cloud credentials wallet credentials production secrets private browser sessions production infrastructure unless explicitly authorized and protected. ================================================== AUTONOMY LEVELS LEVEL 0 — READ ONLY LEVEL 1 — SAFE LOCAL OPERATIONS LEVEL 2 — SANDBOXED INSTALLATION LEVEL 3 — SANDBOXED EXECUTION LEVEL 4 — EXTERNAL SERVICE INTERACTION LEVEL 5 — PRODUCTION DEPLOYMENT LEVEL 6 — DESTRUCTIVE OPERATIONS ZERO_APPROVAL means pre-authorized safe operations can happen automatically. It does NOT mean unrestricted destructive access. ================================================== ARTIFACT SYSTEM Artifact fields: artifact_id task_id type mime_type location checksum size created_at retention visibility tenant_id metadata provenance license source Track provenance: model/version tool/version worker/version prompt/config source materials transformations dependencies license task timestamps ================================================== VIDEO PIPELINE PATI should eventually support: story script scene decomposition character bible image generation image-to-video voice generation lip sync sound music editing QA final video Independent scenes should be parallelized when possible. The orchestration system should ultimately return one finished video artifact. ================================================== RESEARCH ENGINE The research engine must be evidence-oriented. For every technology: Technology Purpose Free? Open Source? Self-hostable? API? GPU required? Kaggle compatible? Commercial use? License Limitations PATI role Confidence Last verified ================================================== COMPETITOR RESEARCH Research: Cocodly Lovable Bolt v0 OpenHands Pythagora Aider Goose Claude Code Codex ecosystem Gemini CLI Also discover other relevant free/open-source tools. Compare: purpose capabilities API self-hosting free availability pricing limitations ownership vendor lock-in what PATI can replace what PATI should integrate with what PATI should avoid Paid services can be studied for comparison but MUST NOT become required PATI dependencies. ================================================== DATABASE Core entities: users tenants roles permissions capabilities tools models workers providers adapters tasks jobs artifacts benchmarks quotas events logs policies agents secrets_metadata health_checks deployments Use migrations. Do not hard-code providers into orchestration. ================================================== MULTI-TENANCY Design from the beginning for: tenant_id user_id roles permissions quotas resource policies artifact visibility audit logs API keys service accounts Single-user mode can be the default. The architecture must remain compatible with future SaaS/API deployment. ================================================== OBSERVABILITY Track: request_id trace_id task_id worker_id model_id tool_id adapter_id tenant_id timestamps latency resource usage errors retries quota consumption artifact IDs decision logs Provide health endpoints. ================================================== TESTING Required: unit tests integration tests adapter tests routing tests policy tests security tests schema tests worker tests Kaggle tests artifact tests MCP tests API tests browser tests end-to-end tests failure-recovery tests benchmark tests Every adapter requires: health test minimal execution test error test timeout test cleanup test metadata test ================================================== FAILURE RECOVERY Support: timeouts retries exponential backoff worker replacement model replacement tool fallback checkpointing artifact preservation partial-result handling quarantine circuit breakers health degradation quota exhaustion handling Never fabricate successful results. ================================================== DEPLOYMENT Separate: CONTROL PLANE from: COMPUTE PLANE CONTROL PLANE: API authentication authorization orchestration routing registries database observability policy COMPUTE PLANE: local workers Kaggle workers containers GPU workers media workers coding workers research workers ================================================== FREE INFRASTRUCTURE Investigate legitimate $0 infrastructure options. Categories include: free notebook compute free GPU compute free CPU compute free hosting free databases free storage free networking free deployment open-source self-hosting browser execution community compute Verify every service. Do not assume something is permanently free. Build replacement paths. ================================================== OPEN SOURCE AND LICENSE POLICY Before activating any component: identify license identify commercial-use permissions identify redistribution restrictions identify model-specific restrictions record source record version record verification date reject incompatible components Never assume open source automatically means unrestricted commercial use. ================================================== PATI API Core API concepts: GET /health GET /capabilities GET /models GET /tools GET /workers POST /tasks GET /tasks/{id} POST /tasks/{id}/cancel GET /tasks/{id}/logs GET /tasks/{id}/artifacts GET /artifacts/{id} GET /quotas GET /system/status POST /research POST /tools/discover POST /tools/install POST /workers/register POST /workers/{id}/jobs Exact endpoint naming may be refined during implementation. API responses must be versioned and schema validated. ================================================== JSON SCHEMAS Create: schemas/capability.schema.json schemas/tool.schema.json schemas/model.schema.json schemas/worker.schema.json schemas/job.schema.json schemas/task.schema.json schemas/artifact.schema.json schemas/provider.schema.json schemas/policy.schema.json schemas/tenant.schema.json schemas/user.schema.json schemas/agent.schema.json schemas/adapter.schema.json schemas/benchmark.schema.json schemas/health.schema.json All must be valid JSON Schema. ================================================== REQUIRED DOCUMENTATION Create: README.md MASTER_PRD.md AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md GEMINI.md CODEX.md CURSOR.md COPILOT.md ARCHITECTURE.md API_SPEC.md MCP_SPEC.md DATABASE.md SECURITY.md AUTH.md MULTI_TENANCY.md TOOL_REGISTRY.md MODEL_REGISTRY.md CAPABILITY_REGISTRY.md WORKER_SPEC.md KAGGLE_WORKER.md LOCAL_WORKER.md ROUTING.md QUOTA_MANAGER.md AUTONOMY.md TOOL_DISCOVERY.md ADAPTER_SPEC.md SANDBOX_SPEC.md POLICY_ENGINE.md ARTIFACT_SPEC.md EVENT_SYSTEM.md OBSERVABILITY.md LOGGING.md TESTING.md BENCHMARKING.md EVALUATION.md FAILURE_RECOVERY.md DEPLOYMENT.md DEV_ENVIRONMENT.md CI_CD.md FREE_FIRST_POLICY.md LICENSE_POLICY.md OPEN_SOURCE_POLICY.md COMMERCIALIZATION.md MULTI_TENANT_SAAS.md ROADMAP.md IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md RESEARCH_REPORT.md ================================================== JSON / DIRECTORY STRUCTURE Design a clean repository structure around: /apps /packages /adapters /workers /agents /schemas /docs /tests /scripts /config /artifacts Refine the exact structure after research. ================================================== IMPLEMENTATION PHASES PHASE 0 Research + environment audit. PHASE 1 Repository foundation. PHASE 2 Core API. PHASE 3 Capability registry. PHASE 4 Model registry. PHASE 5 Tool registry. PHASE 6 Local worker. PHASE 7 Kaggle worker. PHASE 8 Task orchestration. PHASE 9 Intelligent router. PHASE 10 Quota manager. PHASE 11 Artifact system. PHASE 12 MCP. PHASE 13 Personal AI integration. PHASE 14 Research engine. PHASE 15 Autonomous tool discovery. PHASE 16 Adapter generation. PHASE 17 Coding agents. PHASE 18 AI media pipelines. PHASE 19 Multi-tenancy. PHASE 20 Commercial SaaS/API packaging. ================================================== IMPLEMENTATION RULE Do NOT create a fake repository filled with placeholder files just to make it look complete. Build real components. After every major phase: run tests validate schemas check imports start the API test workers test security test policies test free-only enforcement record failures fix failures continue If something fails: debug it. If a technology is unsuitable: replace it. If a free service disappears: find another free solution. Do not replace a failed free solution with a paid solution. ================================================== MVP DEFINITION OF DONE MVP is complete only when: API starts health works capability registry works model registry works tool registry works worker registry works task submission works routing works worker execution works validation works artifacts work logs work quotas work failure handling works safe MCP works Personal AI integration works schemas validate security controls work tests pass no paid AI API is required ================================================== AUTONOMOUS INFRASTRUCTURE MANAGER The finished PATI system should be able to determine: What capability is required? What tools/models can provide it? Which options are genuinely free? Which options are legally usable? Which options can run on available hardware? Which worker should execute the job? Is quota available? Can the tool be safely installed? How did it benchmark? Is it better than the existing option? Should it replace the existing option? What artifact was produced? What happened if execution failed? These decisions must be based on: registries policies evidence health checks benchmarks historical performance ================================================== COMMERCIALIZATION Eventually PATI should support: hosted SaaS private enterprise deployment API platform self-hosted edition managed worker network AI infrastructure marketplace workflow automation media-generation backend coding-agent backend However: COMMERCIALIZATION MUST NOT CREATE A PAID DEPENDENCY IN THE CORE SYSTEM. Users may eventually pay ME for access to MY API. That is different from PATI requiring me to pay another AI company. ================================================== CRITICAL AUTONOMY RULE I want PATI to be highly autonomous. It should be able to: discover tools research tools evaluate tools install tools configure tools test tools benchmark tools register tools replace tools remove failed tools discover models evaluate models route tasks manage workers manage quotas recover from failures maintain adapters run tests monitor infrastructure But autonomy must remain inside security boundaries. ZERO_APPROVAL does not mean unrestricted access. ================================================== QUALITY BAR Do not build: a simple AI wrapper a hard-coded provider integration a single-model system a single-cloud system a paid API dependency a fragile demo a collection of disconnected scripts Build: AN AI INFRASTRUCTURE LAYER. ================================================== FINAL ABSOLUTE RULE NEVER RELAX THE $0 REQUIREMENT JUST TO MAKE SOMETHING WORK. If you discover a paid service: DO NOT USE IT AS A CORE DEPENDENCY. If you discover a free alternative: RESEARCH IT. If the free alternative has limitations: DESIGN AROUND THEM. If several free alternatives exist: COMPARE THEM. If one fails: REPLACE IT. If all free options fail: RETURN RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. DO NOT ASK ME TO PAY. DO NOT ACTIVATE BILLING. DO NOT USE PAID CREDITS. DO NOT HIDE COSTS. DO NOT MAKE PAYMENT A REQUIREMENT. ================================================== FINAL EXECUTION COMMAND You are now responsible for PATI as: AI infrastructure architect software architect research engineer security engineer DevOps engineer MLOps engineer agent-systems engineer API designer database architect QA engineer benchmarking engineer technical researcher START WITH PHASE 0. Do not begin by giving me a generic explanation. Perform the actual research. Determine the strongest legitimate $0 technologies currently available. Verify their capabilities and restrictions. Research current free infrastructure. Research current free/open models and tools. Research Kaggle and other legitimate free compute options. Research the relevant coding agents and AI infrastructure. Research the current API, MCP, worker, model-serving, deployment, and orchestration options. Produce the research findings. Produce the implementation decisions. Produce the architecture. Then begin implementation. Continue through the phases as far as realistically possible. Test what you build. Fix failures. Find alternatives. Do not stop because one component fails. Do not substitute paid infrastructure. Keep everything aligned with: COST = $0 The ultimate objective is: BUILD MY OWN AI INFRASTRUCTURE. BUILD MY OWN API. MAKE IT CAPABLE OF SERVING MY PERSONAL AI. MAKE IT CAPABLE OF EVENTUALLY SERVING OTHER USERS. KEEP THE CORE INFRASTRUCTURE FREE. KEEP IT MODULAR. KEEP IT REPLACEABLE. KEEP IT SECURE. KEEP IT AUTONOMOUS. KEEP IT OPEN TO BETTER FREE TECHNOLOGIES. DO NOT MAKE ME PAY. START NOW. END PATI COMPLETE MASTER PROMPT
